title: EGLD 4h: −16.5% drop, then 4–5 days of a tight rising channel with 3 touches on each line. How much do you trust this flag?
author: FarInspector1873
selftext:
EGLD/USDT, 4h (Nov 14–19).

After a drop of about 16.5% on heavy volume, price has spent roughly 4–5 days in a gentle rising channel. Both lines have 3 touches, which is more than most flags I see. Price is now at the lower line around 2.55, with the upper line near 2.70, and volume has been far below the drop.

The textbook read is a bear flag, but the channel is very tight and slow, and I've seen similar structures turn out to be bases.

Questions I can't settle:

* Do 3 touches on each line make the pattern more reliable, or is that just a coincidence?
* Would you wait for a 4h close below the lower line, or enter on a failed retest of the top?
* Is a slow, light-volume grind more bearish than a sharp bounce, or less?

How do you handle flags that last this long?

Not a call, just a chart I'm following.

comments.author: robbyedit
comments.body: What has this got to do with AI ?

replies.author: FarInspector1873
replies.body: Fair point, I should have framed it for this sub. The channel lines and touch counts came from an automated pattern-detection scanner, not from hand-drawn lines. I'm curious how people here think about this kind of tool: do you trust algorithmic pattern detection, or do you still check everything by eye? And would you want a model to judge whether a flag like this has worked historically, rather than just flagging it?
